outcome.note:
All remaining arc-surface contracts landed in storytree-ai/storytree: #101 Work states at increment and arc grain (1.4–1.6); #103 Agents on the board (2.1–2.4); #105 Waits (4.1–4.4); #108 Briefing (5.1–5.3); #112 the read-only overlay and in-app proofs (3.1–3.6). These extend the original #35 part states and #37 live reading in packages/arc-surface. The desktop mounts the package view over the forest, carries public library reads, and invokes its smoke check. The collision fence was respected; no forest-folder mount remainder is left.

Each capability followed committed red then green, with every commit pushed and CI merging each non-draft PR after Linux, macOS and Windows passed. Final local verification passed typechecking and all 12 test units under the heavy lock. Actual desktop-renderer acceptance with isolated Postgres and headless Chromium verified live claims (1.84 s), clock-only idle, retries, every lifecycle scope, preserved question folds/scroll, live settlement, read-only actions, and returning to the same forest on Close/Escape. Evidence is in packages/arc-surface/evidence; the lane report is /tmp/arc-surface-report.md. No product work remains in this increment. The owner can use pnpm desktop:smoke on the laptop to inspect the native desktop capture; this headless box's acceptance is recorded.

One earlier Windows library teardown failure was recorded as friction arc-surface-windows-cloud-cleanup-permission; subsequent fresh-main verification passed without modifying or skipping the library tests. No owner decision is required. No claims or successor sessions were taken by this lane, as directed.

fields.body:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `storytree-0-3-arc-surface-arc-inc-01`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

This is the owner-gated first step, as it was for the library and the agent link (ADR-0625 D5). Draft the arc surface's capability tree:
- each capability in two plain sentences;
- what it depends on;
- how it will be proven, red then green;
- a simple diagram of how the parts connect.

The owner reads best from a private artifact page with a short Python sketch and an office analogy that says where it breaks.

**Put it to him, then END.** Author it as an `open-question` on this arc: `pnpm storytree question new --arc storytree-0-3-arc-surface-arc … --pg`. Never wait while holding a claim. Three reviews are being drafted at once (verified health, the arc surface and the forest), and he answers them one at a time, in his own order. That was the owner's selection on 2026-09-26: "Draft all 3 now, answer 1 at a time". So a draft may wait in his queue, and that is expected.

**Questions the tree must answer:**
- How each story's planned, in-progress or landed state is derived from the records: claims, landings and health.
- How "by which agent" is shown, from the agent link's sessions and claims.
- How it shares the project switcher with the forest (`storytree-0-3-forest-arc`), whose review is being drafted at the same time.
- The one 0.2 render not to port, recorded in `0-3-arc-surface`'s body: a row waiting on the owner must never also read as takeable.

**Read first:**
- ADR-0625: D3 story 3, and D8 (no increments in 0.3).
- ADR-0626, the agent link's sessions and claims.
- ADR-0621, the library API: `projectTree`, `arcsFor`, `changesSince` and `listProjects`.
- In the 0.3 repo (`C:\code\storytree03`): `stories/agent-link.md` and today's plain list in `apps/desktop`.
- 0.2's arc view is reference only: port behaviour, not code.

**When he approves:** record the tree as an ADR and settle the question in the same landing. The build is `0-3-arc-surface`, on this arc.

**Residue (2026-09-26, session "Draft the 0.3 arc-surface capability-tree review", branch `claude/dazzling-ramanujan-15fd62`).** The review is drafted and put to the owner, and this increment now waits on his answer.
- **The question:** `oq-0-3-arc-surface-capability-tree` (now revision 4), on this arc. The owner's readable copy is the private page https://claude.ai/artifact/N8tuscjiftPadHGDJFkLjP, updated in place.
- **Revision 2, same day, after the owner's first read**, in his words: "B and D make sense, 2 and 3 feel like one capability for agent claims to the board - why did you think unplanned activity needed its own. arcs page should probably arcs surface and probably should also have 5 folded into it? what are your thoughts". He did not approve the tree yet. B1 and D1 are his.
- **Revision 3, same day**, for two reasons:
  - The owner dropped verified health from the MVP (ADR-0630), so choice C was reframed. C1, recommended, shows the agent's own report only, labelled as the agent's, and does not draw the verified column.
  - The owner asked: "what about arc dependencies? or have we not scoped that for MVP". That became choice F. They are not in the MVP; 0.3 records only part-to-part dependencies. F1, recommended, shows those, across stories too, adding one proof to Arc surface.
  - The verified-health lane's note, prepended to the question's statement at 09:38, is carried into revision 3's text.
- **Revision 4, same day:** aligned with the forest review the owner approved (ADR-0632).
  - The switcher, the Forest | Arcs toggle and the opening project moved to the new 0.3 app story (`storytree-0-3-app-arc`, ADR-0632 D4).
  - "Unplanned activity" is renamed "unclaimed work" (ADR-0632 D5).
  - C3 now follows the forest drill-down's rule (storytree's column only where something wrote it).
- **The tree now proposed:** three capabilities, built in the order 1 → 3, with 14 contracts in all:
  1. Work states: planned, in progress or landed, for each part and each story, from the log's claimed and landed lines.
  2. Agents on the board (revision 1's "Who is on it" and "Unplanned activity" merged): who holds each part, read through the agent link's own claim reading (harness, when the window opened, reason, active or idle), plus edits made with nothing claimed (unclaimed work).
  3. Arc surface (revision 1's "Arcs page" with "Live feed" folded in): the per-project page, grown out of today's plain list. It shows the agent's own health report (C1), and each part names the parts it waits on, in any story (F1). It stays current through the app's live reading: the main process opens the agent log beside the library and uses `changesSince`, the log's cursor and a once-a-minute re-judge.

  "approve" now takes C1, E1 and F1. A, B (B1) and D (D1) are settled by his first read.
- **Boundaries agreed with the sibling lanes on 2026-09-26** (by message; both sessions confirmed):
  - **Forest** (approved as ADR-0632, whose D3 records these):
    - Work states (1) and the arc surface's live reading (part of 3) are this tree's, and the forest uses them. It reads Work states per part. In revision 1 these were "Work states (1) and Live feed (5)"; the forest session was told the new names.
    - Whichever view lands first retires today's plain list, and whichever lands second adds the Forest | Arcs toggle, under the 0.3 app story's name.
    - If the forest lands first, it builds these under this tree's names.
    - Both views show the same cross-story part dependencies, and both say "unclaimed work".
  - **The 0.3 app** (new story, ADR-0632 D4, arc `storytree-0-3-app-arc`): it owns the switcher, the toggle, hosting the views and which project opens first. This tree uses its switcher, and both views use today's dropdown until it is built.
  - **Verified health:** the boundary agreed with that lane (it would write only the verified column, with a "checking" note) no longer applies. The owner dropped verified health from the MVP (ADR-0630), and its lane closed with nothing built.
- **If he approves:**
  - Record the tree as an ADR in his words (`adr new --decided`).
  - Settle the question in the same landing (`question settle … --adr <n>`).
  - Write the tree up as `stories/arc-surface.md` in the 0.3 repo, and build `0-3-arc-surface` red→green in the order 1 → 3, landing through pull requests.
- **If he reshapes it again:** revise the question in place as the next revision, and republish the page at the same URL.
- **Reading `arc show` meanwhile:** 0.2's arc view prints both "waiting on the owner … held" and "`active` but NO claim holds it … Takeable" for this increment. That is exactly the 0.2 render this story exists not to port. The waiting line is the true one: nothing here is work to take until he answers.
- Nothing was built and nothing was committed (ADR-0625 D5).

**Owner, round 3 (2026-09-26, on revision 4), verbatim:** "should be a overlay over the forest is that still what we going for, we dont need to reinvent this from 0.2 the arc surface was working quite well in 0.2. I want arc dependancies and increment dependancies in the MVP i think its important. Any more questions?"
- **Settled by it:**
  - E: the arc surface is an OVERLAY over the forest, as 0.2's arc surface was a top-drawer lens over the map. This replaces E1's separate view with a toggle.
  - Port 0.2's arc surface behaviour: one lane per arc, a bar per unit, queued arcs nested under their blocker, a briefing panel for the selected arc, and read-only.
  - F: arc dependencies AND increment dependencies are in the MVP (F2 widened). **ADR-0628 D6**, decided the same day and missed by revisions 1–4, already fixes the 0.3 grain:
    - a story on one arc can wait on a story on another arc;
    - it shows as queued until that story lands;
    - the wait releases on landing, and keeps holding (and says so) if the blocker was retired unlanded;
    - loops are refused when written;
    - the wait is kept apart from code dependencies.

    Arc waits port ADR-0523's arc gate. Both need the library to store them (an extension to its capability 4, the work model) and the agent link's planning tools to set them (an extension to its capability 6).
- **Put back to him in chat:**
  - **Q1.** 0.3 records no open questions. Should the overlay's briefing show only the arc's description, or should 0.3 gain questions that agents raise and settle, shown yellow as "waiting on you"? Recommended: gain them, since cutover moves 0.3's own reviews into 0.3.
  - **Q2.** Does a story's wait refuse an agent's claim on its parts, the 0.3 analogue of ADR-0628 D3's start refusal, or only show? Recommended: refuse, naming the blocker.
- **Next:** revision 5 after his answers. The likely tree is Work states, Waits (new), Agents on the board, and Arc surface (the overlay, with lanes). When recorded, the overlay annotates ADR-0632 D3/D4's "Forest | Arcs toggle" in place, and the app story's review hosts an arcs overlay rather than a toggle.

**Owner, round 4 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "isn't an arc made up of increments, where did this arc is a list of stories come from? Yes open questions should also make it to 0.3 mvp. Yes refuse the claim."
- **Answered:**
  - Q1 = (b): open questions are in the 0.3 MVP.
  - Q2 = (a): a wait refuses the claim, naming the blocker.
- **Provenance he asked for:**
  - "Arc = a list of stories" entered through ADR-0621. Its option B1 settled only that stories belong to the project and an arc MAY list them. Its D6 "left out" list then named "arc increments", a line the drafting session wrote.
  - ADR-0625 D8 spelled out the consequence ("no separate increments inside 0.3"). The signed spec page listed it among the changes his signature covered. He never chose it in his own words.
- **Put back to him:** bring increments back into 0.3 (an arc holds increments, as in 0.2)? Recommended yes. It would:
  - reverse ADR-0625 D8 and ADR-0621 D6's "arc increments" exclusion;
  - return ADR-0628 D6's 0.3 grain to increment-waits-on-increment.

  It would add an increment record and a question record to the library, plus planning, gate, question and claim tools to the agent link. The arc surface's bars would become increments, a straight port of 0.2's lanes.

**Owner, round 5 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "yes bring increments back. Is there anything else we have decided to bring back in only bits for 0.3? just want to make sure theres nothing unintentional i've signed off on"
- **Decided:** increments come back into 0.3 (an arc holds increments). This reverses ADR-0625 D8 and ADR-0621 D6's "arc increments" exclusion, and returns ADR-0628 D6's grain to increment-waits-on-increment.
- **Audit answered in chat.** Every 0.3 decision (ADR-0621 to ADR-0632) was checked for 0.2 behaviour taken only in part through agent-written lines. Flagged for his pick:
  1. decision status and supersession (ADR-0621 D6);
  2. decision numbers (ADR-0621 D6);
  3. the knowledge kinds left out (ADR-0621 D6);
  4. arcs' lifecycle and fields (the ADR-0621 schema);
  5. 0.3's own stories and decisions written as repo files and copied in by `pnpm seed:library`, against ADR-0621 D6's "the library is the only copy";
  6. increment claims (ADR-0626 D9; returns with increments);
  7. no command line for people (ADR-0621 D6, ADR-0626 D9);
  8. a 0.3 librarian that ADR-0631 relies on and nothing schedules;
  9. claims not ending on a PR merge (ADR-0626 D9);
  10. which parts of increments and questions return (for revision 5).
- **Next:** revision 5 after his picks.

**Owner, round 6 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "All 9 need to be brought in, cuts should only be made by explicit decision by me, 0.2 worked well we shouldnt cut the parts that worked into bits, it should be easy to bring this stuff over as I'm sure we exposing our builders with the ability to refer to 0.2 code and corpus to bring it over."
- **Recorded as ADR-0633** (accepted, load-bearing in effect).
  - D1: no cut without his explicit decision; an agent-written "left out" line is only a proposal.
  - D2: builders port from 0.2's code and corpus.
  - D3: 14 items back in the MVP whole, including increments, open questions, arc and increment waits, a wait refusing a claim, and the arc surface as an overlay.
  - D4: every other agent-written cut is in `oq-0-3-cuts-awaiting-owner-decision` on `trusted-circle-distribution-arc`.
  - D5: routing, parked as four increments: `0-3-library-tree-for-adr-0633`, `0-3-agent-link-tree-for-adr-0633`, `0-3-library-is-the-one-copy` and `0-3-librarian-home`.
  - In-place notes in ADR-0621, 0625, 0626, 0628, 0631 and 0632, written by a librarian subagent in the same landing.
- **This session handed over at the context mark** (711K of the ~700K soft mark). Revision 5 is for a FRESH session.
- **REVISION 5 BRIEF (for the next session on this increment):**
  - **Port 0.2's arc surface WHOLE, as an overlay over the forest** (until the forest lands, over today's plain list). Read the behaviour from 0.2's code:
    - `apps/studio/src/components/ArcSurface.tsx`, `apps/studio/src/lib/arcSurface.ts` and `packages/arc/src/arc-rollup.ts`;
    - ADR-0314 (lanes and briefing), ADR-0523 (arc gate, nesting), ADR-0574 (waiting on the owner, yellow), ADR-0628 (increment gates) and ADR-0564 (what a close meant).
  - **What the port carries:**
    - one lane per arc, one bar per INCREMENT (arcs hold increments again);
    - lane states: waiting on the owner, blocked, claimed, unknown, quiet, parked and closed;
    - queued arcs nested under their blocker;
    - a briefing panel with the arc's description and open questions;
    - claim chips per arc, read-only, kept live.
  - **Settled and still binding:**
    - D1: idle never reads as free;
    - B1: in progress means started and not landed, now at increment grain too;
    - a wait refuses a claim (enforced by the agent link);
    - Work states and the live reading stay shared with the forest (ADR-0632 D3).
  - **Still open for him:** C (health beside the state; C1 recommended). E and F are superseded by the overlay and ADR-0633.
  - **The tree must follow `capabilities-name-durable-functions-decisions-go-on-shelves`,** and put every remaining 0.2 piece not ported as a NAMED choice (ADR-0633 D1).
  - **Agree boundaries** with the library's and the agent link's tree revisions above.
  - **Revise `oq-0-3-arc-surface-capability-tree` in place as revision 5,** and republish its page at https://claude.ai/artifact/N8tuscjiftPadHGDJFkLjP. Fetch its current HTML with the Artifact tool's read action on that URL, then publish back with `url`.


**Owner, round 7 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "C0, A". He typed it in the drafting session (desktop title "Draft the 0.3 arc-surface capability-tree review"), choosing from two options that session composed, and that session relayed it to revision 5's session by message; the words were checked against its transcript.
- **C0:** no health on the overlay, as in 0.2. Health stays with the forest (its leaves and drill-down, ADR-0632). Choice C is closed.
- **A:** 0.2's increment lifecycle is kept, and a proposal counts as waiting on the owner. The option text said 0.2 shows a proposal "yellow beside open questions (ADR-0359)". 0.2 as built does not: a proposal draws grey, its lane does not read waiting, and its briefing's proposal list was cut at the owner's word in 0.2 ("I never read the proposals so we should drop that part of the surface"). Revision 5 records A as he read it (yellow, listed under "Waiting on you", lane reads waiting) and gives him a one-word exit, "A as built".

**Residue (2026-09-26, session `sleepy-wright-b57669`, branch `claude/pensive-wilson-369e7b`): revision 5 is drafted and put to the owner.**
- **The question:** `oq-0-3-arc-surface-capability-tree`, revised in place (store seq 21129). His readable copy is https://claude.ai/artifact/N8tuscjiftPadHGDJFkLjP, now version 6.
- **The tree:** five capabilities and 23 contracts, built 1 → 2 → 3, then 4 and 5:
  1. Work states: parts (revision 4's rule, which the forest reads), increments (one reading, first match: waiting on the owner, then queued, then held, then open) and arcs (0.2's seven lane states, in 0.2's order);
  2. Agents on the board: who holds each increment and part, live or idle. Unclaimed work moved to the forest (its capability 6);
  3. Arc surface: the overlay itself, a lane per arc and a bar per increment, counts never a percentage, lane chips, Active/Parked/Closed, and the live reading;
  4. Waits: queued arcs fold under their blocker, and queued increments name their blocker;
  5. Briefing: the intent, then open questions and proposals under "Waiting on you", then settled questions with their answers.

  Work states is still capability 1 and the live reading still part of capability 3, so ADR-0632 D3's references hold.
- **Open for the owner:** Q, a queued increment's colour (Q1, 0.2's queued-arc clay, recommended) and L, the floor-health lamp (ADR-0314 D7; L1, later, recommended). "approve" takes Q1, L1 and every proposed book.
- **Boundaries:** aligned with the forest (ADR-0632) and the app (ADR-0634). The library's and agent link's sides are PROPOSED and written onto `0-3-library-tree-for-adr-0633` and `0-3-agent-link-tree-for-adr-0633`, because no session held either. The main proposals: the library owns the one reading of whether a wait holds and whether an increment waits on the owner; the agent link's refusal also covers work waiting on the owner.
- **When he approves:** record the tree as an ADR in his words (`adr new --decided`) and settle the question in the same landing. Annotate ADR-0632 D2 in place: its "Cross-story capability links are shown, the same ones the arc surface shows" no longer holds, because the overlay shows increments, not part links. Write `stories/arc-surface.md` in the 0.3 repo. The build `0-3-arc-surface` needs the library's and agent link's revised trees for increments, questions, waits and increment claims; Work states at part grain (what the forest's capability 2 reads), and the live reading, need neither, so they can start first.
- **If he reshapes it:** revise the question in place as revision 6 and republish the page at the same URL.
- Nothing was built and nothing was committed (ADR-0625 D5).

**Owner, round 8 (2026-09-27), verbatim, in session `sleepy-wright-b57669`:** "Follow 0.2, a proposal shouldnt wait for my yes, proposal means not built yet doesnt mean waiting on me, else I end up having to say "build it" to things i directed to be built."
- **A is settled as 0.2 has it:** a proposal means not built yet. It draws grey, is not listed in the briefing, and never makes its arc read waiting. "Waiting on the owner" means only work held on a question he has not answered (ADR-0574).
- **Revision 6** records it (store seq 21148; page version 7, same URL). It withdraws revision 5's proposals that the agent link refuse a claim on an unapproved proposal and ready a proposal only on his say-so. The boundary notes on `0-3-agent-link-tree-for-adr-0633` and `0-3-library-tree-for-adr-0633` are corrected to match.
- **Still open:** Q and L. The residue above otherwise holds, reading "revision 6" for "revision 5".

**Owner, round 9 (2026-09-27), verbatim:** "increment waiting on other work should show up yellow. whats the floor hearlth lamp?"
- **Q is settled:** an increment that cannot start because of a wait (its own, or its arc's) draws yellow, like work held on his question; the hover names what it waits for. 0.2's clay bar colour for a queued arc is not used; the lane's arrow and "blocked" chip still show a whole arc waiting. Revision 7 (store seq 21161; page version 8).
- **L is the one choice left.** He asked what the lamp is; it was explained in chat and he has not decided.

**Owner, round 10 (2026-09-27), verbatim:** "bring it back later it needs rework anyway, in 0.2 i never really saw it light up and never really use it, the concept is right the implementation needs rework"
- **L is settled:** the floor-health lamp is neither in the MVP overlay nor cut. It is parked on this arc as `0-3-floor-health-lamp-reworked`, for after first users, with its own review before code.
- **Revision 8** (page version 9) has every choice settled. What remains is his approval of the tree ("approve"). When it comes: record the tree as an ADR in his words, settle the question in the same landing, annotate ADR-0632 D2, and write `stories/arc-surface.md` (see the residue above).

**Owner, round 11 (2026-09-27), verbatim:** "for increment state can we get rid of withdraw and closed these should be folded into red - red is anything that failed to complete or was not completed. Yellow is waiting or blocked. sessions/agents claim the whole arc right not sure why we have increment level agent holds?"
- **Decided:** four increment colours. Green landed; red anything not completed (failed, withdrawn, closed with nothing recorded); yellow waiting or blocked; grey open. The record keeps the kind of close (ADR-0564) and the hover shows it. Revision 9 (store seq after 21167; page version 10). Proposed with it: lane chips "waiting" and "blocked" yellow.

*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `increment-gates-arc-inc-02`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

**The owner asked for this in 0.3 too** (2026-09-26): first "also have it in 0.3 when that part of it gets built", then "i just asked it [the arc-surface session] to start looking at arc dependancies so it makes sense to also include this increment feature in 0.3". ADR-0628 D6 records the behaviour to carry. The 0.2 code is reference only, because 0.3 ports behaviour, not code: `packages/arc/src/arc-rollup.ts` (`incrementQueuedBehind`, `arcGatesOf`) and `packages/arc/src/arc.ts` (`waitGraphOf`, `startRefusal`).

**The behaviour, at 0.3's grain.** In 0.3 an arc is a list of stories (ADR-0625 D8), so the wait sits between stories:
1. A story can name another story, on its own arc or another, that it waits for. The edge lives on the WAITING story. The blocker names nothing, so "what does this hold up" is a query.
2. It is its OWN edge, not the story's code or knowledge dependency. Two graphs that draw the same picture get read as one, and a schedule read as depth cannot be spotted from the view (ADR-0523's argument).
3. It releases only when the blocker LANDS. That is derived from the blocker's own recorded close, never a stored flag, so a landing releases the waiter with no write to it. A blocker that closed without landing (withdrawn or failed) keeps holding and names the fix: re-point the wait at the replacement, or release it. A blocker that cannot be found is a permanent wait, never a release.
4. On the surface, a waiting story reads QUEUED, never takeable. It names what it waits for and on which arc, and the blocker's row says what it holds up. The counts stay disjoint, in the order: waiting on the owner, then queued, then held by a session.
5. Loop refusal happens at WRITE time, over ONE graph covering story waits AND arc-level waits together. The two kinds can close a loop that neither sees alone: story A on arc X waits on B on arc Y, while Y is queued behind X.
6. Where it binds: in 0.2, `arc increment start` refuses while any wait holds, whether the increment's own or its arc's. The 0.3 analogue is an agent claiming a story through the MCP tools, which may belong in whichever tree owns claiming (the agent link?).

**Where it enters: this arc's capability tree**, which the owner approves before any code (ADR-0625 D5). Revision 1 of the review (`oq-0-3-arc-surface-capability-tree`) did not include these waits. Fold them into the tree the owner is reviewing now, beside the arc dependencies he asked this arc's session to look at. That can be a capability of its own, or part of "Work states", your call.

**How it got here.** It was parked on `increment-gates-arc` (the 0.2 build, PR #2095) and re-homed to this arc on 2026-09-26. Two direct messages to this arc's review session expired before they were approved, so this row is the channel that does not depend on anyone approving anything.

**Close it** as landed once the approved tree includes the waits, pointing at the ADR that records the tree: `pnpm storytree arc increment close increment-gates-arc-inc-02 --note "<the ADR>" --disposition landed --pg`. If the owner declines or defers it, close it as withdrawn with his words.

**Separate from the 0.3 design: waits between the 0.3 plan's own increments in the 0.2 store.** Now that PR #2095 is merged, the 0.2 store can hold waits the 0.3 increments' own wording already states:
- cutover's four blockers;
- install waiting on cutover;
- first users waiting on install and the forest;
- each build waiting on its review.
Leave out the partial waits on the agent link, because an increment-level wait would hold those builds longer than their wording says. The catch: a session whose checkout predates the merge has its next write to a row carrying a wait refused as SCHEMA SKEW. So write these only once the sessions touching those rows are on post-merge checkouts, or tell them to merge `main` first. Nobody has taken this yet. It fits whoever drives the 0.3 arcs' dependencies, and it is otherwise ordinary work for any session.

fields.body:
Found 2026-09-30 by the arccapture lane (increment_78fcaa473b06), when the repaired main capture harness (packages/arc-surface/evidence/capture.mjs) ran its relaunch check.

**Defect.** On a launch where the drawer was left open on the parked (or closed) scope with an arc picked, the picked arc is lost. packages/arc-surface/src/view/mount.ts:70-71 calls `watchBoard({... kept ...})` and only then `watching.setScope(scope)`. `watchBoard` (src/board/live-board.ts:32) draws synchronously at construction, and with a kept board snapshot (kept-state, #239) that first draw is a real board at scope "active". mount's `draw` then finds the saved `picked` absent from the active lanes, resets `picked` to the active board's default selection and `remember()`s it, overwriting the saved selection before the saved scope is applied. The scope itself survives (mount's own variable); the selection does not.

**Evidence.** In the harness, after opening the drawer, choosing Parked and picking a parked arc, the saved storage reads `{"open":true,"scope":"parked","picked":"arc_…"}`; the relaunched page shows Parked pressed but the parked arc's `aria-pressed` is "false" (capture.mjs, the `open/scope/selection persist across launch` check). With that one assertion commented out every other check passes. See packages/arc-surface/evidence/drawer-shape/relaunch-selection-red.txt.

**Likely fix (not decided here).** Let watchBoard take the starting scope (e.g. `scope` in WatchBoardOptions) so the first kept draw is already at the saved scope, or have mount skip selection reconciliation until the scope is applied. Pin it with a unit test in packages/arc-surface (mount or live-board) that goes red on the current order; then the harness's relaunch check goes green and drawer-shape/capture.json can be refreshed.

fields.title: Lanes that wait on other work read "quiet": how should the board show them?
fields.answer: Q1 (question_82a893da8e53): "B - however just to confirm this feels like the surface dynamically reorganuses which i think is the solution, when the arc hits the increment that is dependant on another increment in another arc the  arc automatically moves to be a dependant on that arc. This way the arcs self organise in a way - what do you think?" Q2, on the two prose-only gates: "the other two are gated on specific evets that need to happen that should be placed in the parked surface". Q3, how to park them: selected "Park their whole arcs".
fields.stakes: The arc board is how you tell which arcs can move. Today five lanes read "quiet", which you read as "could proceed but isn't", and in at least three cases that is wrong: the work is waiting on another arc or on you, and the board cannot show it. Your answer decides whether the lane chip rolls up its increments, whether dependent lanes fold under what they wait on, and whether gates written only in prose get recorded.
fields.analogy: An airport departures board. Today a flight with no gate agent at the desk shows "on time" even when its inbound plane hasn't landed. A makes it say "delayed: waiting on inbound"; B also lists it under the inbound flight; C makes the crew write down the reasons they already know ("waiting on catering") so the board can show them. Where it breaks: flights don't depend on each other in chains the way increments do, and nobody parks a flight (D) to tidy the board.
fields.context:
Mock of every option, drawn on your real lanes: https://claude.ai/artifact/A3PEAXJbAAMBuo3dpMnnkF

Why it happens. The lane chip (arcState, packages/arc-surface/src/work-states/board-states.ts) asks only three things of the arc itself: an open question on the arc (waiting), an arc-level wait (blocked), a claim (claimed / idle). Otherwise it says quiet. It never looks at the arc's increments. Increment bars do go yellow when an increment waits on other work or on your answer, but the lane does not pick that up. Separately, some gates exist only as sentences in an increment's text, which nothing reads.

The five lanes this morning:
1. Arc surface: its only open increment (the floor-health lamp) waits on "First trusted-circle users" on the first-users arc. The bar is yellow, the lane says quiet.
2. Cutover: "make 0.2 read-only" says in prose it needs your go-ahead; its recorded wait has closed and its question is settled, so it reads free. Three later calls of yours (archive the 0.2 repo, stop 0.2's database, and the training wheels, which ADR-0745 says have already come off) are prose only.
3. Hosted library: the new-user run on the old Windows laptop says in prose it waits until the laptop is ready.
4. Agent link settings and 5. the 0.2 port: really were unclaimed at that moment; both now have sessions or open questions, so they no longer read quiet.

Terms. A "wait" is a recorded link saying this increment (or arc) cannot start until that one closes. "Queued" is the yellow state an increment gets from a wait. "Claimed" means a live session holds it. The drawer already folds an arc under another arc it waits on (a caret with queue chips), but only for arc-level waits, not increment-level ones.

Any choice narrows the arc states ADR-0638 approved (waiting, blocked, claimed, idle, quiet, parked, closed), so it is recorded as a new decision.

fields.options:
A. Roll the increments up into the lane. If every open increment is held, the lane reads "queued" (yellow) and names what it waits on; if at least one is free and unclaimed, it reads "ready · N to take" instead of "quiet". Sorts with blocked, above claimed. For: one rule change; "ready" becomes a dispatch list. Against: lanes stay flat, the dependency is only a phrase in the chip; does nothing for prose-only gates.

B. A, plus fold a queued lane under what it waits on. Reuse the drawer's existing caret and queue chips so a lane whose every open increment waits on another arc's work sits under that arc (arc surface would appear under "Storytree 0.3 to first users"). For: shows what unblocks what; reuses built parts; the top of the list is live work. Against: a folded lane is hidden until you open the caret; a lane with some work free and some waiting stays top-level; a lane waiting on two arcs folds under one and shows "+1 other wait".

C. Turn prose gates into records, and keep them turned (pairs with A or B). A gate that is your call becomes a question on the arc (lane reads "waiting on you"); a gate that is a thing in the world ("old laptop ready") becomes a small increment the work waits on (lane reads queued). The librarian pass at each landing flags open increments whose text names a gate with no recorded wait or question. For: no new state; fixes the cause. Against: more items on your question list, some standing ("tell me when"); the flag is a judgment pass and can miss phrasing.

D. Reorganise the plan instead. Park any arc whose only open work is gated (the arc surface would move to Parked until first users land). For: no code; shorter list today. Against: kept by hand and drifts; parked work leaves the active view so you lose the "what waits on what" picture; the next arc hits the same problem.
fields.statement: How should the arc board show a lane whose work is waiting on another increment, another arc, or on you, instead of calling it "quiet"? Pick one or more of A–D below.
fields.recommendation: Non-binding: B with C. B (which includes A's roll-up and the "ready" rename) makes the board honest about what it already knows and shows where held work sits; C makes the prose gates visible to it. D is not needed once B folds gated lanes away. After you choose I record the decision, park the build as increments on this arc, and then ask you to confirm what the cutover and old-laptop gates really are before recording them.

fields.title: Running sessions on the forest: quiet claims and a context list
fields.intent: Replace the forest's claim pills with a running-sessions surface the owner can read at a glance. Owner-directed 2026-09-28 after the forest showed three identical red banners ("Claude Code: held for the Mint Codex lane ... · hooks not running") for one supervisor holding three app-setup capabilities: noise that told him nothing. Shaped with him in chat through two mocks: (1) the map keeps only a small dot per piece an agent holds; the reason text leaves the map; "hooks not running" leaves the map entirely (it is a self-check of the forest's own plumbing, always true while 0.3 is driven from 0.2 sessions) and moves to the setup check, while the rule that a hookless holder is never faded as idle stays (ADR-0626 D4's substance kept, its display narrowed). - Today the running-sessions list keeps a row only while its session holds a claim, or has a child that does (packages/forest/src/sessions-list/sessions-list.ts, around lines 44-91). That is why rows vanish overnight: a merged PR, a window close or `/clear` ends the claim.

- A session can work in several worktrees (the lines record `folder` per line). Its row shows the worktrees it has worked in, not only the folder its `session-started` line named (readings.ts ~70).

fields.body:
ADR-0749 D3 and D4, superseding ADR-0748's readings-only version.

**Today.** The app computes context bars itself (packages/app/src/surfaces/reads.ts `contextReadings`):
- every 10 s it re-reads the whole activity log from seq 0;
- it opens each session's transcript file from local disk.

So sessions on the Mint box have no bar on the laptop.

**The change.**
- (1) The agent link, on the session's own machine, streams each session's transcript records into the shared store as the session works. It reads from a per-session byte cursor and includes subagent transcripts tied to their parent. Hooks already fire on every tool call and turn end, so the hook can ship the new tail without a daemon.
- (2) Before writing, it scrubs obvious secrets: API keys, bearer/OAuth tokens, private keys, connection-string passwords. Each is replaced with a marker naming what was removed. It is best-effort, and the setup check says so.
- (3) A central parser in our code builds the context composition and the window reading from the stored records. The pure folds `claudeCodeWindow`/`codexWindow` (packages/agent-link/src/context/window.ts) and the composition fold already take transcript text with no I/O, so only their `readFile` wrappers (`sessionWindow`, `contextReading`) swap source.
- (4) Retention: raw records older than 180 days are deleted, and the derived readings are kept.

**Red first:**
- a session run on machine A is drawn with a bar and a window by an app that has no access to A's transcript file;
- a planted fake key in a tool output is stored as the marker, not the key;
- a record older than 180 days is gone after the retention pass, while its derived reading remains.

**Also check:** the bar's 700K/850K ticks are hard-coded (sessions-list.tsx ~130), while the context-guidance default is now 600,000 (settings.ts:12). Confirm whether they should agree.

**Consumer:** the owner, reading bars and windows for every machine's sessions in one list. The same stored records are also the base for later features.

fields.body:
ADR-0749 Consequences. There are two ways the shared log can mislead once everything reads from it.

(1) **Lines are lost when the store is down.** Hooks write nothing if the store is unreachable within 2 s (hooks.ts ~61, 121-122, 148-150): the machine asleep, a network blip, a store restart. Nothing backfills the gap.
- Add a small local queue under [home] that the next successful hook uploads.
- It must keep the original times and order. It must never duplicate a line (give each line an id and upload idempotently).

(2) **A crashed window never ends.** A window that dies without `session-ended` stays idle for ever.
- Add a "gone" state after a long silence (a setting, default suggested 12 h, the same as LONGEST_COMMAND_MS).
- A gone session is hidden like an ended one, but read as "stopped reporting", never as "ended".

Red first:
- a line written while the store refuses appears after the store returns, exactly once;
- a session silent past the limit is hidden and reads as gone.

Consumer: the owner, trusting that the list neither drops live sessions nor keeps dead ones.
fields.title: No lost lines, no stuck sessions
fields.objective: A local queue replays hook lines written while the store was down, and a long-silent session reads as gone

fields.body:
Operational follow-up to #227/#229/#230 (ADR-0749).

**The problem.** Streaming (#229) and queued lines (#230) live in the HOOKS. Both machines' user-level hooks still run from detached agent-link checkouts that predate those PRs:
- laptop: `C:\code\storytree03-wt\agent-link`, at c0a79ef (2026-09-28 14:22);
- Mint: `[home], at 46244a0 (2026-09-28 17:35).

The app follows main and now reads bars and windows only from the shared store. So on 2026-09-29 the sessions list showed every session with an EMPTY bar, except the build lane that had shipped its own transcript by hand while verifying.

**The recipe.** It is owner-approved (question_6bdc148e3443, option B), and is done per machine, in that machine's agent-link checkout:
1. Back up `[home] (and the Codex hooks config).
2. `git fetch origin && git checkout --detach origin/main`
3. `pnpm install`
4. `pnpm --filter ./packages/agent-link build`
5. `node packages/agent-link/dist/storytree-setup.mjs install`
6. Diff settings.json against the backup: only storytree's entries may change.
7. `node packages/agent-link/dist/storytree.mjs doctor`. The doctor should also name the best-effort scrub, which is new in #229.

On Mint, the Codex hooks wait on one interactive `codex` trust prompt (owner step).

**Done when:**
- a session STARTED AFTER the reinstall, on each machine, shows a filled bar in the laptop app;
- rows exist in `transcript_records` for it.

Sessions already open keep the old hooks until restarted.

Merge lookup extends claims/merges.ts from claim branches to every branch a session's lines name; deletion/ahead-of-main via git.
- A session with open work stays listed, marked as holding unmerged work.
- Desktop session = its id is in the app's own record: Claude `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude-code-sessions\<acct>\<org>\local_*.json` (`cliSessionId`, `isArchived`; also `archived-sessions.idx`), Codex `[home] threads (`id`, `archived`, `archived_at`, source not exec). Never decide by `entrypoint`. Work resolved -> dimmed "done"; archived -> removed (unless open work); session-ended does not remove it.
- On each machine the agent link reads that state and writes `session-archived` / `session-unarchived` lines. Read-only against the apps' files; fail soft and say so in the setup check.
- Other sessions: removed once work is resolved AND (session-ended OR a new quiet-time setting beside `idle-after`, default 12 h, counted from resolution or last line, whichever is later). Replaces the hardcoded 12 h gone rule.

Verification, recorded 2026-09-29 by the Mint build lane (session f81c0768):
(a) Does archiving a running Claude desktop session fire SessionEnd? UNVERIFIED. The desktop app is not on the Mint box. The Claude Code 2.1.284 CLI's SessionEnd reasons are clear, resume, logout, prompt_input_exit and other, with no archive reason; that does not settle what the desktop app does when it archives. Needs a look on the laptop. D4 does not depend on it: a desktop session's session-ended never removes it anyway.
(b) Does Codex's terminal UI have an archive? YES. codex-cli 0.153.4 has `codex archive <session>` and `codex unarchive <session>` for saved sessions, over the same [home] `threads.archived` / `archived_at`. On the Mint box that table holds 110 `exec` threads and 293 subagent threads (source is JSON `{"subagent":…}`), none archived, and no interactive thread. So the reader treats every Codex thread in state_5 that is neither `exec` nor a subagent as the app's own (the increment's "source not exec"), terminal or desktop alike; both can be archived.
(c) Why did the Mint box end only 3 of 13 sessions? Claude Code kills SessionEnd hooks after 1.5 s by default (AbortSignal.timeout(1500) in 2.1.284; CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS or a per-hook timeout up to 60 s raises it). Our Claude SessionEnd hook is synchronous with no timeout and must first connect to the Cloud SQL library, which takes about 2.4 s from the Mint box; killed, it never reaches its enqueue fallback (queued-lines is empty). Every Mint session since 2026-09-27 is a detached `claude -p` that shut down normally. Fix parked as its own increment on this arc: increment_23ee753572b1.

Found 2026-09-29 while verifying ADR-0754 D4 (c) on the Mint box ("why did the Mint box end only 3 of 13 sessions"). Evidence, read-only:
- Every 0.3 session on the Mint box since 2026-09-27 is a detached headless `claude -p` (transcript entrypoint `sdk-cli`), and their transcripts end in a normal shutdown (`stop_hook_summary` with no hookErrors, then `cost-state`), so they were not killed.
- Claude Code 2.1.284 does fire SessionEnd in print mode, but runs SessionEnd hooks under `AbortSignal.timeout(1500)` by default (raised by `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS` or a per-hook `timeout` in seconds, up to 60 s). Read from the strings of [home]
- Our Claude SessionEnd hook is registered synchronously with no timeout (setup/hooks-config.ts claudeEntries: `SessionEnd: [{ hooks: [run(false)] }]`), and before writing it connects to the library: a read-only `storytree arc list` against the Cloud SQL library took 2.37 s and 2.49 s here. So the hook is aborted at 1.5 s before it appends `session-ended`, and a killed hook never reaches its enqueue fallback ([home] is empty).
- The laptop went 7 of 7; not measured why (probably a faster connect).
Fix: register Claude's SessionEnd with `--background` (the hand-off Codex's Stop and PreToolUse already use: the hook hands its input to a detached copy and exits in milliseconds), and/or give it `timeout: 10`. Red first: a SessionEnd hook run under a 1.5 s kill still lands its `session-ended` line.
Side finding: every hook on the Mint box runs from a dev worktree's build (`[home]), so rebuilding or removing that worktree would silently break all hooks there (see increment "Reinstall hooks from main on laptop and Mint").

fields.body:
The context bar sorts each record into Injected, Grounding, Implementation or Other by its bytes ÷ 3.8 (composition.ts CHARS_PER_TOKEN). An image block (a Read of a PNG, a screenshot) sits in the transcript as base64, so a 1.1 MB screenshot counts as ~300K tokens while the model pays ~1.5K for it (Claude images cost about width×height/750 tokens, the long edge resized to at most ~1568 px, so ≤ ~1.6K each).

Measured 2026-09-29 on the laptop: the session behind PR #263 (transcript 19f80731…) showed ~1,021K Grounding, of which ~1,006K (99%) was 10 screenshot Reads; everything else it read was ~15K. Every frontend and evidence session's bar is inflated the same way.

Fix: count an image block at its cost, not its base64 length: read the PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP header for its size, apply the harness's resize and w×h/750; when the size cannot be read, a fixed ceiling (~1.6K). Applies to Claude Code and Codex readings alike (view_image). Test first: a transcript with one large image Read reads as ~1.6K Grounding, not hundreds of K.

fields.body:
Found 2026-09-30 by session c56faf99 while cleaning the factory floor. The owner asked: "is there a reason the session surface shows 13 active sessions with unmerged work?"

Measured on the laptop (packaged 0.3.309, Cloud SQL library) at ~22:30 UTC 2026-09-29: `storytree session list --json` had 28 listed sessions with open work, holding 90 "open work" branches. Checked against GitHub (`gh pr list --state merged --limit 1000`) and git (after `git fetch --prune`):
- 14 had a merged PR (not yet resolved by the list)
- 74 exist nowhere: no local branch, no origin branch (never pushed, e.g. claims held for library-only work or for Mint lanes that pushed under another branch; or deleted after merge)
- 1 was the asking session's own branch, +0 over main
- 1 was a lane in flight
So zero sessions held real unmerged work, yet 13+ read as active with open work.

Causes (packages/agent-link/src/sessions/branch-states.ts, called from hooks.ts ~line 172):
1. Throughput: resolveBranches runs at most once a minute per project per machine, with a 3-second budget, and each branch costs a `gh` call (~1 s on Windows). That's about 2-3 branches a minute, only while some session's hooks fire. A quiet factory never drains, and a 90-branch backlog needs about 40 minutes of continuous hook traffic.
2. Unreachable: a branch's "deleted / nothing ahead" is asked only of git on the machine its lines were written on, in the folder they name or the nearest one still there. Lines written on the Mint box ([home]) are only resolvable there, and the box still runs a #230 source build without this code. Sessions whose folders are gone (C:\code\storytree03-wt\supervisor-0927, orient-0928) depend on the nearest-folder fallback.
3. The "merged" check needs a PR whose head is that branch. A claim branch that was never pushed can only resolve through the local deleted/+0 check, which is cause 2.

Want: the list reads a branch as resolved when it exists nowhere (no local ref on any machine that has it and no origin ref), not only when the original machine checks it; and the backlog drains in one pass (one `gh pr list --state merged` for all branches instead of one call per branch), so a quiet factory's list is true within a minute of the next hook. Pin red: a session whose only branches are (a) merged by PR and (b) absent locally and on origin is no longer listed with open work after one resolve pass. Test-first per ADR-0623.
fields.title: The sessions list shows finished sessions as holding open work: branches resolve too slowly, and absent branches never do

outcome.note: Branches now resolve in one pass: one gh call lists every merged PR, and a branch worked on only elsewhere resolves as deleted once neither origin nor this clone has it (its own machine reopens it if still there).

fields.objective: A session whose branches are merged or exist nowhere drops out of the open-work list within one resolve pass

fields.body:
Found 2026-09-30 by laptop session 712ceb5b when the owner asked why the app showed 11 active sessions while only 2 were running.

Symptom. The sessions list counted 11 finished sessions as at work: each had closed out "safe" after its PR merged (#264–#279), yet read "says safe, but <branch> is unmerged" and so needs-you (ADR-0758 D3). GitHub showed every branch merged.

Fault 1: no machine had written a branch-state line since 2026-09-29 12:57 UTC. packages/agent-link/src/sessions/branch-states.ts resolveBranches runs from the hook (packages/agent-link/src/hooks/hooks.ts, after endMergedClaims, "never at a session's end"). The Mint box wrote them until its lanes stopped. The owner's laptop (Windows, hooks from the installed app: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\storytree-0.3\resources\agent-tools\storytree-hook.mjs, built 2026-09-30 00:57) has NEVER written one: no storytree-merges-storytree.stamp / storytree-branches-storytree* in %TEMP%, though its hooks append lines fine. Run by hand from a 0.3 worktree, resolveBranches wrote the missing states at once (gh pr list returned 278 merged PRs in ~2 s), so the logic works and the hook path on Windows does not reach it or fails silently. Suspects to check first: the BACKGROUND hand-off (hooks.ts `flags.includes(BACKGROUND) && handOff`) returning before the merge block, a different tmpdir or PATH (no gh) in the handed-off process, or the bundled agent-tools build missing the call. Find it with a test that goes red for the real cause.

Fault 2: packages/agent-link/src/readings.ts sessionsFrom computes openWork only from branch-state lines, ignoring the `merged` line endMergedClaims already writes for a claim's branch (e.g. claude/increment-11bc9a126beb-eb2336 had `merged` at 13:08:47 but still read unmerged). A branch named by a `merged` line (with no later work on it) should read resolved.

Done: resolveBranches was run once by hand on 2026-09-30, so the live count now reads right; this increment keeps it right.

Fence: packages/agent-link. Acceptance: a Windows laptop session's hooks write branch-state lines for merged branches within a couple of minutes (check with the laptop after landing: the owner's app updates itself at a quiet moment), and a session whose only branch has a `merged` line is not listed as holding open work.
fields.title: Merged branches stop reading unmerged: laptop hooks record merges, and a merged line counts

fields.body:
﻿The sessions list read merged branches as unmerged a second time (2026-09-30): 15 closed-out sessions read "says safe, but <branch> is unmerged" though every branch was in origin/main. Cause: the list trusts branch-state lines that only a hook's look around the machine writes, and no hook had written one since 02:53Z. PR #280 moved the look into a 20 s hand-off, but hooks run from the installed desktop app (v0.3.309 on the laptop, pre-#280), which updates only while it runs, so the fix never reached the hooks. Run by hand, resolveBranches cleared all 25 branches in 6.7 s.

The hooks run from the installed desktop app's bundle and update only while the app runs. On 2026-09-30 the laptop's hooks were v0.3.309 while v0.3.333 was out, so PR #280's fix never ran and no hook recorded a merge for 7 hours (friction_f42b5554bbad). Make hooks current without the app open (e.g. the hook, or storytree setup, fetches the latest release's agent-tools when behind), and have the setup check / sessions list say when the running hooks lag the latest release. Related: increment_80678e768757 (reinstall by hand).

OWNER'S ANSWER 2026-10-01 (question_44555a5ee60d, option A): start the desktop app at sign-in, in the tray, so its updater runs all day and the hooks it installed follow each release within minutes (CI cuts a release after nearly every merge: v0.3.394 to v0.3.402 in four hours on 2026-09-30). Not B (hooks do not download releases themselves) and not a checkout take-over (question_b51dc00dfc08 answered NO; increment_94f88db1040f withdrawn). The lag report (contract 8.18, option C) already landed and stays.
What to build: the desktop app registers itself to open at sign-in, hidden in the tray (Electron app.setLoginItemSettings with openAtLogin and a start-hidden argument, or the equivalent the app's installer supports), on by default for installs, with a way to turn it off in the app's settings; starting at sign-in opens straight to the tray with no window. This is lifecycle, so it belongs in the thin frame (apps/desktop) per ADR-0649. Red test first on the frame's login-item decision (a fake for the Electron call). Windows only matters today (the updater does not run on Linux; the Mint box follows main). Proof on the laptop (sign out and in, see the tray icon, hooks follow the next release) is the owner's to watch, not a question.


RESIDUE 2026-10-01 (Mint lane 'autostart', session 602fb3f1): BUILT AND GREEN, NOT MERGED. PR storytree-ai/storytree#372 (branch claude/increment-ba6f0d9b9c98-25124d): the installed Windows app registers an Electron login item ('storytree 0.3' under HKCU Run, launched with --background = tray, no window), on by default; the gear's Updates section has an 'Open at sign-in' switch whose choice is kept in [home]; dev copies, portable builds, runtime slots and smoke runs never register (same installedApp() check as the release updater); the uninstaller (not an update) deletes the Run value. Contract app lifecycle 1.12 (contract_ba624f1c6c17), tests in apps/desktop/src/main/sign-in.test.ts; pictures in apps/desktop/evidence/sign-in/. Verify on Linux, macOS, Windows all PASS; CI's automerge step fails enqueueing ('Resource not accessible by personal access token', question_8522ccce492a). NEXT: once the MERGE_QUEUE_TOKEN is fixed, run `gh run rerun 36786091919 --failed`, watch #372 reach MERGED, then close this increment landed --pr 372. Live check on the laptop (sign out and in, tray icon, hooks follow the next release) is the owner's to watch.

fields.objective: storytree noticeboard log can show one line's full command (by its sequence number, or with a flag that stops truncation), so an investigation needs no throwaway script against the activity log's API

fields.body: Friction drain 2026-10-02. Evidence friction_aced72a5e114 reports a fresh claimed worktree and branch deleted before the first edit after PR #500 close-out. Independently confirmed: readings.ts:547 reopens a close-out only on prompt-submitted or a non-compact session-started; new claimed lines do not reopen it. worktree-reaper.ts:75 selects every session with closeOut.verified, allowing clean fresh HEAD already in main to be reaped. Add the smallest product regression: after verified close-out, a new admitted claim makes the session active again and prevents reaping the fresh worktree before any code edit; then close-out/reaping still works when the new work truly finishes. Claims/Sessions path only; no blanket suppression of the reaper. New code needs a fresh claimed worktree outside the st03-resteer fence. Supervisor owns dispatch; this slot only routes the concern.
fields.title: A new claim reopens a closed-out session

outcome.note:
PR #508 repairs the close-out/claim handoff. A new admitted claim invalidates the session's earlier close-out, so the session is listed again and the reaper cannot delete its newly claimed clean worktree before any edit. Releasing the new claim and genuinely closing out again still allows normal cleanup. The reaper's eligibility rules are unchanged; the separately blocked activity-log-line increment was not built.

Red commit 1633490e reproduced deletion of the fresh claimed worktree. Green commit a8f7bc11 fixes the shared session fold. The real Postgres/git regression and existing close-out/reaper tests pass; pnpm run gate --guidance passes typecheck, all 16 package units, guidance and plan edges. Existing platform-only and live Cloud SQL skips remain explicitly unverified locally.

The opening incident's pending-command detail was investigated against its activity log: session 01a0fab1-8d4f-7d50-9e29-f68745ad60d8 recorded close-out #52308 at 2026-10-02T04:01:07.993Z and admitted claim #52330 at 04:01:43.146Z, 35.153 seconds later. Pending CLI completion did not mean a later close-out event. The deleting process for that incident was not independently identified; both remedies are covered by the demonstrated stale-close-out repair.

Contract 4.12 and ADR-0758 were corrected in place; ADR-0790 now links to ADR-0758. Friction and health drains and graduation were empty. No owner question or implementation residue remains in this increment. Opening continuation belongs to the supervisor's queued lane, which may retry its fresh workspace after merged hooks are registered on Mint. No successor session was started.

fields.objective: A continuing session can claim its next fresh worktree without its previous safe close-out authorizing the reaper to delete that worktree.

fields.title: Look at the filled sessions list (hooks first)
fields.answer: Option D, reads wrong in two ways. Hooks were already reinstalled from main (22:44 on 2026-09-28) and live bars fill once a session acts. After looking at a mock of fuller bars (0.2 session 15cdda8c), the owner said: "can you show me a mock one thats more full, so i can see what this would look like for a session that has quite a full context window. from what i can see it needs a color legend so i can see what the bar colors mean", then: "add the legend in the header and widen the bar to 120px". Carried by increment "Sessions list: colour legend in the header, bar widened to 120px" on arc_895e232031b0. The scale (1M), ticks and colours stand as built.
fields.stakes: The arc's end state is your look at the live list; without a hooks reinstall on this laptop every bar stays empty, so the look cannot happen.
fields.context:
Landed on arc_895e232031b0 by session 78fef608 on 2026-09-28: #184 (bars and totals line up), #185 (the agent link's context reading carries its composition in four groups, contract 9.8), #187 (ADR-0737: off-plan removed, capability 6 retired, claim reasons held to 40 characters, contract 5.16), #188 (bars filled from the reading: app surfaces 3.5, forest 7.6).

Terms. A "context reading" is how many tokens a session's context holds, worked out from the transcript file its hooks named (agent link capability 9). "Composition" is how those tokens split into the four groups, estimated from the labels the harness puts on each transcript record. "Hooks" are the small commands Claude Code runs on each event, which write the activity lines the forest reads; they are registered in [home]

Scale choice (made in #188, open to your look): the bar spans 1,000,000 tokens on every row, so rows compare; a reading has no window size (ADR-0728), so this is only the display's scale. Claude marks at 700K (the guidance default, ADR-0729) and 850K (ADR-0557).

Evidence: a Chromium capture of the list with synthetic readings is at packages/forest/evidence/sessions-list-alignment/rows-1440.png. A real Claude Code desktop transcript (270,549 tokens) split as injected 56.7K, grounding 35.9K, implementation 70.0K, other 132.5K.

Known limits: Codex rows have no composition yet (one raw segment); subagent rows have no reading of their own and show "—".
fields.options:
Step 1, the hooks (pick one):
A. You reinstall them: from a checkout at current main, run the storytree setup your agent setup uses (storytree setup install). Your settings, your hands. Analogy: swapping the batteries in a meter before reading it; it breaks down in that the old batteries still "work", they just miss one wire.
B. Tell the next session "yes, reinstall the hooks from main" and it will run the install for you. Faster for you, but it rewrites your global Claude Code settings on your say-so.

Step 2, the look (after the hooks and the app update):
C. It reads right: the arc's end state is met and it can close.
D. It reads wrong: say what (for example the 1M scale, the colours, the 65px bar width, the 40-character limit), and each becomes an increment on this arc.

Non-binding recommendation: A or B, then C or D as you see it. The scale is the call most likely to need your taste.
fields.statement:
Does the running-sessions list now read right? Look at the bottom-left Sessions panel in the desktop app once #187 and #188 have merged and the app has updated itself: every row's bar and total in one column, no "off plan" badge, names of 40 characters or fewer, and each bar filled with its session's context use in four colours (grey Injected, blue Grounding, amber Implementation, muted Other), numbers on hover, Claude rows marked at 700K and 850K, Codex rows one grey segment.

Before the bars can fill with real numbers, one setup step is needed on this laptop: the Claude Code hooks installed in your user settings run an old build (2026-09-26, at C:\code\storytree03-wt\agent-link\packages\agent-link\dist\storytree-hook.mjs) that does not record where each session's transcript is. fields.title: Look at the live sessions list: does the legend and 120px bar read right?
fields.answer: Q1 A: reads right, including the wider panel (525px).
fields.stakes: This look is the arc's end state: a yes closes the running-sessions arc; a no names what still reads wrong and becomes the next increment. One call beyond your words is also yours to confirm: the panel grew 55px wider.
fields.analogy: Like adding a key to a chart and making the chart wider: the page had to grow a little so the labels beside it didn't get squeezed. Where it breaks: the panel floats over the forest, so a wider panel covers slightly more of the map.
fields.context: Checked in Chromium at 1440 and 420px wide: legend colours equal the segment colours (they share one definition, so they cannot drift), every bar is 120px, bars and totals line up in one column, the header stays inside the panel. At 470px a 40-character name measured 249px against a 238px column, which is why the panel widened. Under 600px wide the bar is 59px and the legend wraps under the title. Screenshots: packages/forest/evidence/sessions-list-alignment/rows-1440.png and rows-420.png.
fields.options: A: Reads right, including the wider panel. The arc's end state is met and the arc can close.\nB: Reads right, but keep the panel at 470px and let long names cut off with an ellipsis instead. One small follow-up increment; the claim reason limit (40 characters) would then no longer guarantee a whole name.\nC: Something else reads wrong (say what); it becomes the next increment on this arc.
fields.statement: Your answer to question_6bdc148e3443 is live (PR 202, merged 2026-09-28; the desktop app restarted into it at 23:42). Open the storytree app's forest and look at the Sessions panel, bottom left. The header now reads 'Sessions N' with four colour keys to its right (Injected grey, Grounding blue, Implementation amber, Other muted), in the same order and colours as the bar segments. Each row's bar is 120px wide (was 65px); scale (1M across), the 700K/850K marks and hover numbers are unchanged. To keep a 40-character session name whole (the claim reason limit is 40 because names that long fit), the whole panel grew by the same 55px, 470 to 525px, instead of the name column shrinking. Does the list read right?
